title: Synchronous vs asynchronous replication

kcs.statement: With synchronous replication the leader acknowledges a client's write only after the configured set of replicas has acknowledged it. An acknowledged write survives leader failure as long as one of those replicas still holds a durable copy and failover promotes a replica that has it. The cost is that every write waits for the slowest required acknowledgment and stalls when a required replica is unavailable.
With asynchronous replication the leader acknowledges a write immediately and ships it to followers afterwards, giving low write latency but losing the not-yet-replicated writes if the leader dies.
